draft.title: Hypotheses and investigable questions
card: Investigable question
a question that can be answered by collecting data, such as by measuring or counting. It often asks how changing one thing affects another.
Not investigable
a question about opinion or taste, such as which colour is nicest, cannot be answered with measurements. Neither can a question about what someone should do.
Hypothesis
a testable explanation that predicts what will happen if it is right. It is often written as: if we change this, then that will happen, because of this reason.
Testing it
an investigation collects data to test the hypothesis. The data may support it or not. A hypothesis must be able to be shown wrong.
draft.remember: Investigable questions can be answered with data. A hypothesis is a testable prediction with a reason.

a.q: A class wants to plan an experiment. Which question could they answer by collecting data?
opts: How does water temperature affect how fast sugar dissolves?
Which flavour of ice cream tastes the nicest?
Should schools have longer lunch breaks?
Is blue a better colour than green for a uniform?
a.why: Dissolving time can be measured at different water temperatures, so data can answer the question. The other three depend on opinion or on what people think should happen, so measurements cannot settle them.
a.clue: Which question could you answer by measuring something?

b.q: Mia grows bean plants in a Dubbo school garden. She thinks plants given more sunlight will grow taller, because they can make more food. Which is the best hypothesis for her investigation?
opts: If bean plants get more sunlight, they will grow taller
Do bean plants grow taller in more sunlight?
Bean plants are the nicest plants to grow at school
Sunlight is important for all of the living things
b.why: This one predicts what will happen if the idea is right, and it can be tested by measuring height. The question asks something but makes no prediction. The other two are an opinion and a vague claim that cannot be tested.
b.clue: A hypothesis states a prediction rather than asking something.

a.best: How does water temperature affect how fast sugar dissolves?

b.best: If bean plants get more sunlight, they will grow taller
